questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: If I had studied harder at school, I wouldn't be struggling with this job now.
If I studied harder at school, I wouldn't be struggling with this job now.
If I had studied harder at school, I wouldn't have struggled with this job now.
If I had studied harder at school, I won't struggle with this job now.
questions.explanation: Mixed conditional: If + past perfect (past condition), would + base verb (present result): 'If I had studied..., I wouldn't be struggling now.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Students will keep falling behind unless schools won't provide more support.
Students will keep falling behind unless schools provide more support.
Students will keep falling behind unless that schools provide more support.
Students will keep falling behind without schools provide more support.
questions.explanation: 'Unless' means 'if...not' and is followed by an affirmative clause: 'unless schools provide more support.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Several new courses has been introduced this year.
Several new courses have introduced this year.
Several new courses have been introduced this year.
Several new courses have being introduced this year.
questions.explanation: Present perfect passive: have/has been + past participle: 'have been introduced this year.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: This outdated curriculum should updated immediately.
This outdated curriculum should being updated immediately.
This outdated curriculum should be update immediately.
This outdated curriculum should be updated immediately.
questions.explanation: Modal passive: modal + be + past participle: 'should be updated immediately.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence. (Direct: "Please submit your assignments on time.")
options: The professor told us to submit our assignments on time.
The professor told us submit our assignments on time.
The professor said us to submit our assignments on time.
The professor told us that submit our assignments on time.
questions.explanation: Reported commands: tell + object + to + base verb: 'told us to submit our assignments on time.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence. (Direct: "You should review your notes daily.")
options: She suggested to review our notes daily.
She suggested reviewing our notes daily.
She suggested me reviewing our notes daily.
She suggested that I reviewing our notes daily.
questions.explanation: 'Suggest' is followed by a gerund or 'that + subject + base verb': 'suggested reviewing our notes daily.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The scholarship which she applied for it covers full tuition.
The scholarship for that she applied covers full tuition.
The scholarship for which she applied covers full tuition.
The scholarship she applied for which covers full tuition.
questions.explanation: In formal style, the preposition moves before 'which': 'the scholarship for which she applied.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The report publishing last week revealed a decline in literacy rates.
The report published last week reveal a decline in literacy rates.
The report which published last week revealed a decline in literacy rates.
The report published last week revealed a decline in literacy rates.
questions.explanation: A passive meaning reduces 'which was published' to the past participle alone: 'The report published last week...'

questions.topic: Modal verbs of past deduction (must have)
questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The student must have forgotten about the deadline.
The student must forgotten about the deadline.
The student must have forget about the deadline.
The student must has forgotten about the deadline.
questions.explanation: Past deduction: must have + past participle: 'must have forgotten about the deadline.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The school should acted sooner to address the bullying.
The school should have acted sooner to address the bullying.
The school should have act sooner to address the bullying.
The school should has acted sooner to address the bullying.
questions.explanation: Past regret/criticism: should have + past participle: 'should have acted sooner.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: University tuition fees rose significantly over the past decade.
University tuition fees has risen significantly over the past decade.
University tuition fees have risen significantly over the past decade.
University tuition fees have rose significantly over the past decade.
questions.explanation: 'Over the past decade' links the past to the present, so present perfect is used: 'have risen significantly.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: By the time the exam started, most students already left the hall.
By the time the exam had started, most students already left the hall.
By the time the exam started, most students have already left the hall.
By the time the exam started, most students had already left the hall.
questions.explanation: The earlier of two past actions takes the past perfect: 'most students had already left the hall.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Education ministers are meeting next week to discuss school reform.
Education ministers meet next week to discuss school reform.
Education ministers will meeting next week to discuss school reform.
Education ministers are meet next week to discuss school reform.
questions.explanation: Present continuous expresses a fixed future arrangement: 'are meeting next week.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: She said she will attend the graduation ceremony.
She said she would attend the graduation ceremony.
She said she would attended the graduation ceremony.
She said she would have attend the graduation ceremony.
questions.explanation: In reported speech, 'will' shifts back to 'would': 'she said she would attend the ceremony.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: I wish schools take mental health more seriously.
I wish schools have taken mental health more seriously.
I wish schools took mental health more seriously.
I wish schools would take mental health more seriously as a policy.
questions.explanation: 'Wish' + past simple expresses regret about a present situation: 'I wish schools took mental health more seriously.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: I wish my teachers encouraged me earlier to pursue writing.
I wish my teachers have encouraged me earlier to pursue writing.
I wish my teachers would have encouraged me earlier to pursue writing.
I wish my teachers had encouraged me earlier to pursue writing.
questions.explanation: 'Wish' + past perfect expresses regret about the past: 'I wish my teachers had encouraged me earlier.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: We had our essay proofread by a professional editor.
We had proofread our essay by a professional editor.
We had our essay proofreading by a professional editor.
We have our essay proofread by a professional editor last year.
questions.explanation: Causative form: have + object + past participle shows someone else did the action: 'had our essay proofread.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Never before the university had received so many applications.
Never before had the university received so many applications.
Never before did the university received so many applications.
Never before has the university had received so many applications.
questions.explanation: Negative adverbials at the start trigger inversion: 'Never before had the university received...'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The committee is looking the exam scandal into.
The committee is looking in to the exam scandal.
The committee is looking into the exam scandal.
The committee is looking into to the exam scandal.
questions.explanation: 'Look into' means 'investigate' and is inseparable: 'looking into the exam scandal.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: What students urgently need are a more flexible timetable.
That students urgently need is a more flexible timetable.
What students urgently need is more flexible timetable it.
What students urgently need is a more flexible timetable.
questions.explanation: 'What' clefts take a singular verb when the complement is singular: 'What students need is a more flexible timetable.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Some schools have modern facilities, whereas others still lack basic resources.
Some schools have modern facilities, whereas others still lacks basic resources.
Some schools have modern facilities whereas, others still lack basic resources.
Some schools have modern facilities despite others still lack basic resources.
questions.explanation: 'Whereas' contrasts two clauses and is followed directly by the subject: 'whereas others still lack...'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: In spite the new curriculum, test scores remain low.
In spite of the new curriculum, test scores remain low.
Despite of the new curriculum, test scores remain low.
In spite of the new curriculum, test scores remain low though.
questions.explanation: 'In spite of' is followed by a noun phrase: 'In spite of the new curriculum, test scores remain low.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: A number of studies has linked homework overload to student stress.
The number of studies have linked homework overload to student stress.
A number of studies have linked homework overload to student stress.
A great number of studies has linked homework overload to student stress.
questions.explanation: 'A number of' + plural noun takes a plural verb: 'a number of studies have linked...'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: She spoke in behalf of the entire student council.
She spoke on behalf for the entire student council.
She spoke behalf of the entire student council.
She spoke on behalf of the entire student council.
questions.explanation: 'On behalf of' means 'representing someone': 'she spoke on behalf of the council.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The introduction of smaller class sizes improved student performance significantly.
The introduce of smaller class sizes improved student performance significantly.
The introducing of smaller class sizes improved student performance significantly.
The introduction of smaller class sizes improve student performance significantly.
questions.explanation: Formal writing often nominalizes verbs into nouns: 'introduce' becomes 'the introduction of...'

questions.question: Which is the most appropriate formal opening line for an email requesting information about a scholarship program?
options: I'm writing to ask you about your scholarship program, ok?
I am writing to enquire about your scholarship program.
Just wanted to know about your scholarship program.
Hey, tell me about your scholarship program.
questions.explanation: 'I am writing to enquire about...' is a standard formal opening for information requests.

questions.question: Which is the most appropriate opening line for a formal complaint about unfair grading?
options: I'm writing because I'm really mad about my unfair grade.
I want to complain about my unfair grade, it's bad.
I am writing to express my concern about my grade for this course.
I am writing to express my concern about my grade for this course, ok.
questions.explanation: Formal complaints use measured language such as 'I am writing to express my concern about...'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The results of the national exam were extreme alarming.
The results of the national exam were extremely alarm.
The results of the national exam were very much alarming.
The results of the national exam were extremely alarming.
questions.explanation: 'Extremely' (adverb) modifies the adjective 'alarming': 'were extremely alarming.'

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: Online courses are more flexible. Moreover, they are often cheaper.
Online courses are more flexible, moreover they are often cheaper.
Online courses are more flexible. Moreover they are often cheaper.
Online courses are more flexible moreover, they are often cheaper.
questions.explanation: 'Moreover' begins a new sentence and is followed by a comma: 'Online courses are more flexible. Moreover, they are often cheaper.'

questions.question: Choose the correct question tag.
options: You'd support free university education, didn't you?
You'd support free university education, wouldn't you?
You'd support free university education, would you?
You'd support free university education, wouldn't it?
questions.explanation: A positive statement with 'would' takes a negative tag: 'You'd support..., wouldn't you?'
